London is the largest city as well as capital of England. London had various names like, Ludenwic, Londonium, and Ludenburg, before settling in on the name London. London lies in south-eastern England. London was a small city, For a long time. There were various villages in the city. More people came to live there regularly. Then, the villages combined together into one big city

People

London’s population is 8.63 million.

There are many immigrants in London. These immigrants come from various countries. They speak different-different languages and belong to different cultures and religions.

Landmarks

  • The Millennium Dome
  • River Thames
  • Elizabeth Tower (Big Ben)
  • London Eye
  • Buckingham Palace
  • Tower Bridge
  • London Underground
  • Natural History Museum
  • Palace of Westminster
  • Paul's Cathedral

London Business and Economy

There are five main business districts in London: Westminster, the City, Canary Wharf, Lambeth & Southwark and Camden & Islington. Finance is the largest industry of London which has banks, investment companies and stock exchanges. It also includes professional services like law firms, media (BBC: British Broadcasting Company) and accountants. It is also considered as the largest tourism industry and is the highest visited city throughout the world with 18.8 million international visitors per year. So many technology companies are established in London. It is also considered as the largest retail and the manufacturing center and its retail center contributes approximately tens of billions to the economy of the country

Birmingham is 2nd largest city of the UK. It is a metropolitan area. It is situated at the crossing points of the national motorway and railway systems near the geographic centre of England. In the West Midlands conurbation, Birmingham is the largest city. West Midlands conurbation is one of the principal industrial and commercial areas of England. Birmingham acts as an administrative, recreational, and cultural centre for the West Midlands conurbation. Birmingham is situated in approximately 177 km (110 miles) in the northwest of London.

The Contemporary City

Sometimes, Birmingham is described as “the city of 1,001 different trades.” The diversity of industrial base is the key to economic success if Birmingham because it is mainly concerned with the engineering and metal trades. In terms of employment, its largest single industry is the production of motor vehicles.

Education

The University of Birmingham, University College Birmingham, Aston University, Newman University, and Birmingham City University are the 5 universities of Birmingham city.

Birmingham City Council is the largest local education authority in England. Birmingham City Council is directly or indirectly responsible for the below schools:

Manchester is the main city and metropolitan area in Greater Manchester, England, with a population of 534,982 in 2018 (the fourth most populous district in England). It situated within the second-populated urban area of the United Kingdom with a population of 2.9 million and the third-populated metropolitan area with a population of 3.3 million. The city's local government is the City Council of Manchester. After London and Edinburgh, Manchester is the third most visited city in the UK. It is notable for its architecture, art, cultural exports, media links, performance from engineering and science, sports clubs, transport connections and social impact.

Sport

Manchester is regarded as a sports city. Two famous football clubs in the Premier League bear the name of the city – Manchester United and Manchester City. Manchester United plays their home games at Old Trafford, in Trafford's Manchester suburb, the UK's largest football club ground. Initially built as the main athletics stadium for the Commonwealth Games in 2002, the City of Manchester Stadium was reconfigured into a football stadium prior to the arrival of Manchester City.

Education

Manchester City has three universities:

  • The University of Manchester
  • Manchester Metropolitan University
  • Royal Northern College of Music

Towards northeast of Scotland lies the third most popular city of Scotland, known as Aberdeen. The estimated population of Aberdeen is 196,670. The city was transformed economically after it received the royal burg status between 1124 and1153. The city has two universities namely, University of Aberdeen and Robert Gordon University. While the former was founded in 1895, the latter was given the university status in 1992.

The oil industry and Aberdeen seaport industry have overtaken other industries such as shipbuilding and textiles. The busiest commercial heliport is the Aberdeen heliport.

Transport

Both the domestic and international destinations are served by the Aberdeen airport which is close to Dyce towards the north of the city. The oil industry and rescue services are served by the Heliport which is one of the world’s busiest heliport.

On the main UK rail network lies the Aberdeen railway station. Abellio Scotrail has frequent direct trains to major cities like Glasgow, and Inverness.

Belfast is Northern Ireland's capital and largest city, standing on the banks of the River Lagan on the east coast of Northern Ireland. Belfast is the 12th biggest city in the UK (United Kingdom) and the second biggest on Ireland's island. In 2015, it had a population of 333,871. Belfast suffered greatly from the troubles: it was known to be one of the most violent cities in the world in 1970s and 1980s, with a homicide rate of about 31 per 100,000.

There are two universities in Belfast. Founded in 1845, Queen's University Belfast is a member of the Russell Group, an alliance of 24 UK leading research-intensive universities. Belfast is the first most visited cities in the United Kingdom and the second most visited city on the island of Ireland. In 2008, 7.1 million visitors visited the city.

Brighton is situated 47 miles (76 km) south of London on the south coast of England. Archaeological evidence of the area's settlement dates back to the Bronze Age, Roman and Anglo-Saxon periods. The Domesday Book (1086) documented the ancient settlement of "Brighthelmstone".

Education

The University of Sussex, established in 1961 is a campus science-focused university between Stanmer Park and Falmer, four miles (6 km) from the city centre. The university is house to the reputed Institute for Development Studies and the Science Policy Research Unit, among over 40 other existing research centres, and the World University Ranking ranks 1st in the world for development studies. The University of Brighton, the former Brighton Polytechnic, has 20,017 students, 80 % of are undergraduates.

In 2017 the city was elected as "City of Film" by UNESCO and since then it was a member of the Creative Cities Network. The largest site for the live music is 2,000-seat Colston Hall. The Art gallery and Bristol city Museum have a collection that includes archaeology, real history, local glasswork, artwork and Chinese ceramics.

Cambridge is a university town and county town of Cambridgeshire, England, some 50 miles north of London on the River Cam. The population at the 2011 United Kingdom Census was 123,867, including 24,506 students. During the Roman and Viking ages, Cambridge became an important trading hub, and there is evidence of settlement in the region as early as the Bronze Age. Cambridge is at the center of Silicon Fen's high-tech industry with sectors such as engineering and bioscience and several university-born start-ups. More than 40% of the population has a credential for higher education, more than double the national average.

Cambridge's two universities

  • The collegiate University of Cambridge
  • The local campus of Anglia Ruskin University

State provision includes Hills Road Sixth Form College, Long Road Sixth Form College and Cambridge City College in the further education sector. All public and independent schools educate pupils from nursery to high school age in Cambridge. Cambridgeshire County Council administers state schools, which has a total of 251 schools, 35 of them in Cambridge City.

Cardiff is Wales' capital and its biggest city. It is the 11th largest city in the UK. It is the chief commercial centre in Wales, the basis of most national cultural institutions and Welsh media and the home of the Wales National Assembly. The population of the unitary authority area was measured at 346,090 and 479,000 of the broader urban area. Cardiff was ranked sixth in the world in the alternative tourist destinations of National Geographic.

Economy

As Wales ' capital city, Cardiff is the Welsh economy's main engine of growth. While Cardiff's population is about 10% of the Welsh population, Cardiff's economy accounts for almost 20% of Welsh GDP and 40% of the city's workers are regular in-commuters from the wider southern Wales region. Cardiff is one of Britain's most popular tourist destinations. With BBC Wales, S4C and ITV Wales all having studios in the area, Cardiff is home to the Welsh media and a large media market.

In 2016, the population of Dublin region was 1,347,359. Now, it has an urban area population of 1,173,179. Dublin is famous for shopping area centres upon Grafton Street.

The Global City

Dublin is a contemporary and historical centre for industry, education, arts and administration. In 2018, this city was listed as a global city with a rank of "Alpha" by the Globalisation and World Cities Research Network (GaWC).

Dublin is the main academic centre in Ireland, close to four colleges and several other centres of higher education. Dublin University is the oldest university in Ireland, dating from the 16th century, situated in the centre of the city, and has over 18,000 students. Royal Charter established its single constituent institution, Trinity Institution (TCD), under Elizabeth I in 1592.

The city is the Church of Scotland's annual General Assembly venue. It is birthplace to national institutions such as the Scottish National Museum, the Scottish National Gallery and the National Library of Scotland.

Economy

Edinburgh has the most robust economy in any city outside London in the United Kingdom and the highest percentage of professionals in the United Kingdom, with 43% of the population having a degree or professional qualification. It is the most ambitious large city in the United Kingdom, according to the Center for International Competitiveness.

The city runs 149 primary schools,29 secondary schools and three specialist schools - the Glasgow School of Sport, the Dance School of Scotland and the Glasgow Gaelic School. The city council grants outdoor Education facilities at the Blairvadach Centre.

Leeds is the cultural, financial and commercial centre of the West Yorkshire Urban Area. Leeds was a small manor town in the 13th century and became a major centre for wool production and trade in the 17th and 18th centuries and a major mill town in the Industrial Revolution; wool was still the dominant industry, but flax, engineering, iron foundries, printing and other industries were also important.

There are about 31,000 students at the University of Leeds.

Economy

Despite industrial remnants like Ruston still in place, Lincoln's economy is based primarily on public administration, commerce, arable farming and tourism. Lincoln's main job fields are; public administration, education, and health, which accounts for 34% of the workforce. Distribution, restaurants and hotels make up 25% of the workforce.

Lincoln College, the largest educational institution in Lincolnshire, offers training courses to 18,500 students, of whom 2,300 are full-time. There is also an expert creative college, Access Creative, which offers music, media and games design courses and is available to about 180 full-time students. Luton is a large town, district and unitary area of Bedfordshire, situated in the south-east of England, but for administrative purposes in the east of England. It has a population of 214,109 and is one of the most populated cities without city status in the UK. The town is situated on the Lea River, about 50 km northwest of London. The foundation of the town dates back to the sixth century as a Saxon settlement on the Lea River, from which Luton derives his name. Local museums in Wardown Park and Stockwood Park discuss the history of Luton.

Economy

Traditionally, Luton's economy has centered on a number of different sectors, including automotive, manufacturing and milling. Today, however, Luton is heading towards a service-based economy, mainly in the retail and airport sectors, although there is still an emphasis on the city's light industry.

Education

Luton is one of Bedfordshire University's major locations. A large university campus is in the city center of Luton, with a smaller campus located on the edge of the city in Putteridge Bury, a former manor house in Victoria. The University's other main campus is located in Bedford. There are 98 educational institutions in Luton – seven nurseries, 56 primary schools,13 secondary schools, four new educational institutions and four other educational institutions.

The local authority has been a unitary authority for Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole Council since 1 April 2019. Poole had an estimated population of 151,500, making it the second-largest town in Dorset's ceremonial county. Poole is a tourist resort with a large natural harbour, culture, the Lighthouse Arts Centre and beaches of the Blue Flag, attracting visitors.

The main campus and buildings of the university (Talbot Campus) are within the boundaries of Poole Borough, a smaller campus situated in Bournemouth itself. It offers undergraduate, postgraduate and professional training in creative arts, architecture and media. Media courses are the strength of the university and recent assessments of teaching quality have resulted in ' excellent ' ratings for courses in the areas of communication and media, business and management, catering and hospitality, archaeology and nursing and midwifery.

It is the only island city in United Kingdom, the only city whose population density more than London and the second busiest port in UK after Dover. The tourists attract many forts of the Victorian era on Portsdown hill. The Tudor period Southsea castle and Southern part of Royal Marines are open to the public. The city is home to famous ships: Portsmouth Historic Dockyard, HMS victory. It includes three graves: Kingston, Milton Road, and Highland Road.

It is expected that the Elizabeth line will allow quicker trips to central London. Slough has the highest concentration outside London for global corporate headquarters. Solihull is the richest city in the West Midlands and one of the richest areas outside of London in the UK. The Switch Quality of Life Index named Solihull in November 2013 as the "best place to live" in the UK.

However, Solihull College, was previously known as the Solihull College of Technology, incorporates a University Centre which provides many degree and full degree courses, particularly in technical subjects such as computer science and engineering. Currently, they are 15 secondary schools: St Peter's Academy, Sir Thomas Boughey Academy, Discovery Academy, Ormiston Sir Stanley Matthews Academy, The Co-operative Academy of Stoke-on-Trent, Excel Academy, Haywood Academy, Ormiston Horizon Academy, Birches Head Academy, St Joseph's College, St Margaret Ward Catholic Academy, Ormiston Meridian Academy, St Thomas More Catholic Academy, Stoke Studio College (with sites in Longton and Burslem), Trentham High School and Thistley Hough Academy.

Throughout 2014, City and County of Swansea had a population of 241,300, the second-most populous local authority area throughout Wales after Cardiff, according to its local council. During the industrial heyday of the 19th century, Swansea was the central hub of the copper smelting industry.

Traditional industries mainly steelmaking (British Steel) and chemical manufacture (Imperial Chemical Industries (ICI)), have been primarily replaced by high-tech activities, science development and service sector roles.

A local tradition of textile and tool manufacturing history date back to this time.

The town developed on the Colne River until the 16th century on land belonging to the Abbey of St Albans. A charter was issued to create a market during the 12th century, and the building of St. Mary's Church began. The city grew in part as a result of visitors to Berkhamsted Castle and Kings Langley's royal palace. A palace was built in the 16th century at Cassiobury. This was partially restored in the 17th century and at The Grove was built another country house.

In the northern home counties, Watford is a major regional hub. The county council of Hertfordshire designates Watford and Stevenage as its main sub-regional centres, heading its list of preferred retail sites. The High Street is the main focus of activity at night with a high concentration of bars, clubs and restaurants in the area. The main shopping area is the Harlequin Shopping Centre, a large indoor mall of over 140 stores, restaurants and cafes built in the 1990s, which was officially opened in June 1992.

Windsor is a popular tourist destination as a result of the castle and has amenities usually found in bigger towns: two railway stations, several large hotels, and a theatre. Wokingham was a county until the reorganisation of the local regimes in 1974 when it merged with the Wokingham Rural District to form the new Wokingham District. Borough status has been granted in the year 2007.

The South Western Railway runs the station and offers services including the Great Western Railway. Most of the local bus services are offered by Courtney Buses, but the services from Wokingham to Reading and Bracknell are managed by Reading Buses after First Berkshire & The Thames Valley closed their Bracknell depot in the 2015 summers.

It became a major centre of coal mining, steel production, lock making, and automobile and motorcycle manufacturing in the Industrial Revolution. The city's economy is still focused on manufacturing and the service sector, including a strong aerospace industry.
